title: PHP Sessions
learning_outcomes: Explain what php sessions contributes to a PHP application.

content.intro: Authentication establishes who a user is; authorization determines what that user may do. Secure identity workflows depend on password APIs, session lifecycle controls, expiring tokens, and resource-level permission checks. In this lesson, focus on starting sessions; then compare it with reading session data. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use php sessions when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Authentication establishes who a user is; authorization determines what that user may do. Secure identity workflows depend on password APIs, session lifecycle controls, expiring tokens, and resource-level permission checks. For php sessions, begin with starting sessions. Also distinguish reading session data; updating session state; destroying session data. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.why: A database exposure would reveal the original secrets.
common_mistakes.fix: Use password_hash and password_verify; never design your own password hash.

common_mistakes.why: A signed-in user may not own every resource.
common_mistakes.fix: Check role and resource ownership at every protected operation.

common_mistakes.problem: Keeping the same session identifier after sign-in.
common_mistakes.why: An attacker may be able to reuse a known session ID.
common_mistakes.fix: Regenerate the session ID at authentication boundaries and invalidate sessions on logout.
